overview: This 138-page file gathers U.S. diplomatic, consular, and naval intelligence records on Japanese naval policy and activity from 1931 to 1938. It covers the Shanghai fighting, Japanese forces in Manchuria, alleged Pacific bases, treaty negotiations, fleet expansion, and competing accounts of naval strategy. Translated articles and pamphlets show how Japanese writers argued for naval equality and public support for rearmament.
interest: Diplomatic reports alongside translated Japanese arguments reveal how naval ambitions were assessed abroad and promoted at home.
